ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a gray paper triangle, with vertex A at the lower left, C at the lower right, and B at the upper right. The base AC is labeled 4, the vertical side BC is labeled 3, and the hypotenuse AB is labeled 5, so this is a 3-4-5 right triangle, with the right angle at C. The problem says to fold so that A lands on B, so the points on the crease have equal distances to A and B, and the crease is the perpendicular bisector of line segment AB. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let A=(0,0), C=(4,0), B=(4,3). The midpoint of AB is M=((0+4)/2,(0+3)/2)=(2,3/2). The slope of AB is 3/4, so the slope of the crease is its negative reciprocal -4/3. The crease passes through M, so the equation is y-3/2=(-4/3)(x-2). The other end of the crease inside the triangle falls on AC, that is, y=0. Substituting gives 0-3/2=(-4/3)(x-2), so x-2=9/8, x=25/8. Therefore D=(25/8,0). The crease length is MD: MD=sqrt((25/8-2)^2+(0-3/2)^2)=sqrt((9/8)^2+(12/8)^2)=sqrt(225/64)=15/8.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the image, identify the right triangle with A at the lower left, C at the lower right, B above C, with AC=4, BC=3, AB=5. Place A=(0,0), C=(4,0), B=(4,3). From the text, the fold sends A to B, so the crease is the perpendicular bisector of AB. The midpoint of AB is M=(2,3/2), and since AB has slope 3/4, the crease has slope -4/3. Its equation through M is y-3/2=(-4/3)(x-2). Intersect this line with AC, i.e. y=0, to get D=(25/8,0). The crease segment inside the triangle is MD, so compute MD=sqrt((25/8-2)^2+(0-3/2)^2)=15/8.
